definitions.explanation: The work that came immediately before the current one by the same creator or in the same series — the earlier film, novel, game, or album. Used constantly in reviews and promotional writing.

examples.japanese: {前作|ぜんさく}より{面白|おもしろ}い。
examples.english: It's more interesting than the previous one.

examples.japanese: {前作|ぜんさく}を{見|み}ていなくても{楽|たの}しめる{映画|えいが}だ。
examples.english: It's a film you can enjoy even without having seen the previous installment.

examples.japanese: この{小説|しょうせつ}は{前作|ぜんさく}の{十年後|じゅうねんご}の{世界|せかい}を{描|えが}いている。
examples.english: This novel depicts the world ten years after the previous book.

notes:
{前|ぜん} (previous) + {作|さく} (work). Always relative to a current work, so it appears where a new release is being compared with what came before.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {前作|ぜんさく}に{続|つづ}く: to follow on from the previous work
- {前作|ぜんさく}を{超|こ}える: to surpass the previous work
- {前作|ぜんさく}の{続編|ぞくへん}: a sequel to the previous work

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {新作|しんさく}: new work — the latest release, seen from the other direction
- {代表作|だいひょうさく}: representative work — the piece a creator is best known for
- {続編|ぞくへん}: sequel — the work that follows, not the one that precedes
